title: "RFC 022: Serve Multi-route Enforcement"
subtitle: "Applying RFC 021 Decisions in Code"
date: 2026-01-19
---

## Executive Summary

The RFC 021 decisions are now enforced in the ingestion stack. Queue entries without `route_id` fail fast to avoid ambiguous routing, and strict-mode parsing rejects missing ingestion roots before runtime. New unit tests confirm these guardrails and keep the enforcement behavior deterministic during development.

## Implementation Summary

| Area | Change | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Queue enforcement | Reject pending entries missing `route_id` | `src/autoclean/utils/ingestion.py` |
| Strict parsing | Require ingestion roots to exist in strict mode | `src/autoclean/utils/ingestion.py` |
| Unit tests | Added strict parsing and queue enforcement tests | `tests/unit/utils/test_ingestion.py` |

: Table 1. Enforcement changes and evidence.

## Queue Enforcement

Queue metadata is now treated as mandatory in development. When pending entries lack `route_id`, the dispatcher aborts immediately with a clear error so operators must migrate the queue rather than implicitly reassign work.

::: callout-note
## Guardrail
Pending queue entries without `route_id` are rejected before dispatch to prevent accidental routing across pipelines.
:::

## Strict Root Validation

Serve configuration parsing in strict mode now verifies that each ingestion root exists on disk. This shifts root availability errors to validation time and avoids starting a run that will fail later or silently skip directories.
